history.summary: CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this temple is in KARNATAKA (town Pattadakal), not the value shown in the CSV. The largest and most elaborate monument in the UNESCO World Heritage Group of Monuments at Pattadakal (inscribed 1987). Commissioned c. 740 CE by Queen Lokamahadevi, wife of Chalukya king Vikramaditya II, to commemorate his victory over the Pallavas of Kanchipuram - originally dedicated as the Lokeshwara/Lokeshvara temple in her name; her co-queen Trailokadevi built the adjacent Mallikarjuna (Trailokeshvara) temple. Built in developed Dravidian style, modelled on the Pallava Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram; it in turn served as the model for the Rashtrakuta Kailasa Temple at Ellora. Multi-storey pyramidal vimana, triple mukhamandapas (north, east, south), pillared navaranga, covered pradakshina path, external Nandi pavilion, and densely carved friezes of Shaiva, Vaishnava and epic scenes (Ramayana, Mahabharata, Ravana lifting Kailash, Ugranarasimha, Gajendra-moksha). Pattadakal was the Chalukya coronation site on the west bank of the Malaprabha river. The only functioning shrine in the complex; ASI-managed. name: Virupaksha Temple
town_description: Pattadakal in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, on the west bank of the Malaprabha river, was the ceremonial coronation site of the Chalukya kings. Its group of 7th-8th century temples - blending Nagara and Dravida styles into the vesara idiom - is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987), 23 km from Badami and 10 km from Aihole.

travel.road: 23 km from Badami, 10 km from Aihole; 400 m from Pattadakal bus stand; often visited together with Badami and Aihole
